cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the cake on that spare chair. I'll keep the table clear until everyone has sat down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That leaves one guest without a seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give the guest the piano stool. I'll ask the pianist to stand until it's time for the birthday song.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's time for the song now. The guest has moved the cake onto the table and taken the chair, so the pianist can sit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll cut the cake when the song ends. My clear table has become the serving table, and the spare chair has decided when we're having dessert.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets cake/chair/table order and A3 reallocates stool; A5 resumes control of serving after B rearranges. Objects now cohere, but ordinary successful seating may not distinctly accumulate toward the claimed inevitable dessert consequence.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 missing seat; B4 restores pianist seat through cake/table transfer; A5 uses B4 current song to time serving, with no double occupancy.

relationship.evidence: B2 identifies missing seat and B4 offers an effective guest solution, plausible participation.

heightening.evidence: A5 returns clear table and spare chair in new roles, but serving after everyone sits was compatible with A1 already; claim chair decided timing overstates the chain.

specificity.evidence: A1 cake on chair, A3 guest on stool and B4 cake on table/guest on chair make physical positions explicit.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 final personification explains causality more strongly than dialogue establishes it.

coach2.situation: A1 cake on chair, A3 guest on stool and B4 cake on table/guest on chair make physical positions explicit.
coach2.stated: A1 table clear until seating; B2 guest unseated; A3 guest stool; B4 guest chair/cake table/pianist stool; A5 serves after song.
coach2.inferred: No extra furniture or impossible occupancy now needed. A1 already allowed table use after seating, so final claimed inevitability has limited force.
coach2.missing: No factual gap; distinct culmination remains weak.
coach2.firstDefect: A5 describes a forced outcome where the preceding arrangement mostly fulfills the initial ordinary plan.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 identifies A1 cake placement leaves guest unseated.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 assigns B2 displaced guest piano stool temporarily.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 brings song timing and moves cake/table/guest to restore pianist stool.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 uses B4 song and table arrangement for dessert timing, though that is not clearly forced against A original plan.
